Anna (Platform): Heads-up — hitting a weird propagation delay for private/VPC rollouts. Canary config applied in control plane ~10m ago but customer reports still 100% routing to old model in their VPC.
Raj (Infra): Hmm. Which customer? Any air-gapped constraints? We push control-plane diff to their VPC agent; agent applies locally. Sometimes the agent's outbound sync queue gets blocked by strict egress rules.
Anna (Platform): Customer: SafeBank-prod (air-gapped via proxy). They allow outbound to our control-plane host but only on port 443 and with client cert pinning. No errors in our central logs.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout apply 1763509123 by anna — status: CONTROL_PLANE_ACKED
Sam (SRE): On agent side can we see last applied config timestamp?
Raj (Infra): Yes, agent writes /var/lib/redwood/last_rollout.json and exposes /status. We're seeing apply time 1763506600 which is older — agent didn't pick up latest push.
Anna (Platform): So there's a propagation gap between control-plane ack and agent apply. Is that expected for air-gapped setups? We expected <30s.
Raj (Infra): For always-on agents with healthy network it's low. For air-gapped it's dependent on agent's poll interval + backoff. Default is 5m with jitter. For these customers we could reduce poll to 30s for canaries? But that increases load.
Mike (Product): UX ask: console should show per-customer "agent sync lag" and a per-rollout propagation map. Right now we only show "control plane ack". Customers want visibility of when their edge actually applied the config.
Lisa (Security): If we shorten poll interval for air-gapped agents, need to check cert refresh and mTLS handshake rate. We can't have agents doing full mTLS handshake every 30s for thousands of customers.
Sam (SRE): We could implement a streaming channel (long-poll / websocket) initiated by agent to control plane. For air-gapped, long-lived TLS reduces handshake churn. But proxies may drop idle connections.
Raj (Infra): For customers behind proxies with keepalive drop, long-poll can flake. Another option: agent initiated periodic sync with exponential backoff but with an "on-demand" trigger from control plane when push is pending. That requires a persistent channel or customer-allowed webhook which many don't permit.
Anna (Platform): Operational guard idea: rollout policy should include a "propagation SLO" and an "abort-if-not-applied-by" guard. E.g., traffic split applies only after N% of target agents report applied; else hold split.
Mike (Product): Agree. Quick schema proposal for rollout config:
```json
{
  "spread": "zone-aware",
  "canary": {"pct": 10},
  "propagation": {"max_wait_secs": 600, "required_agents_pct": 80},
  "guards": {"monitor": ["latency","error_rate"], "abort_on": {"error_rate": 2.0}}
}
```
Raj (Infra): Implementing required_agents_pct needs agent heartbeat telemetry and per-customer counters. Telemetry cost increases but we can keep heartbeat tiny (apply_ts + seq + OK bit).
Anna (Platform): Telemetry limited to small heartbeat + apply_ts seems fine. We can route through existing metrics pipeline as a low-volume stream.
Lisa (Security): For air-gapped customers that outlaw outbound telemetry, we need to allow signed telemetry bundles or let ops pull an audit bundle. That adds complexity and a new support flow.
Sam (SRE): Practical fallback: console puts affected rollouts into "Pending apply" state and blocks traffic split beyond canary. Support can trigger a manual on-demand sync via CLI: `redwoodctl rollout sync --customer SafeBank-prod --agent agent-23` or `--all`.
Anna (Platform): Good. Also need a console override with clear risk banner. If a user bypasses propagation guard, we should require admin approval and log it.
Mike (Product): UX: show estimated ETA based on median poll latency per-customer, per-agent counts (applied / targeted), and an explicit "Force apply" action with CLI snippet. Add checkbox: "Allow unsafe override (requires admin approval)".
Raj (Infra): Also consider idempotent per-agent rollout model: sequence numbers, atomic apply + stable rollback. Agent compares seq numbers and only applies newer seqs; rollback is applying an older seq.
Sam (SRE): Agree. Agent should expose /status with fields: seq, apply_ts, pending_ops. We'll add bulk API for per-customer counts: /customers/{id}/agents/status (internal only).
Lisa (Security): For customers that forbid any outbound reachability, default policy should be: mark as "unverifiable" and do not auto-increase traffic. Require manual verification/ops sign-off to proceed.
Anna (Platform): Action items: Raj -> prototype agent push/stream + heartbeat (ETA 2w). Sam -> add apply_ts to /status and bulk status API (ETA 1w). Mike -> mock console UX with propagation SLO and override flows (ETA 1w). Lisa -> review TLS/cert implications and rate limits (ETA 3d). I'll draft an RFC with schema and support playbook.
Raj (Infra): Quick Q — for air-gapped customers who forbid outbound telemetry entirely, do we auto-fail the rollout or mark unverifiable?
Lisa (Security): Mark "unverifiable" and default to conservative: do NOT increase traffic beyond canary until manual confirmation. Require ops sign-off for any override.
Mike (Product): Also add an audit log entry when override happens and a telemetry spike alert if a rollout is forced through.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: task created #3245 "agent-stream-propagation" assigned to Raj.
Anna (Platform): Thanks — I'll draft the RFC and ping folks for review.
